sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Being able to build and run your project reliably — whether on your machine, your colleague's machine, or a CI server — is a baseline expectation in professional development. Maven manages your Java dependencies and build lifecycle; Docker packages your application so it runs identically everywhere. These are table-stakes skills that freshers often lack.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
- **Maven pom.xml** = the recipe for your project: what it depends on, how to build it, and where to publish it.
- **Maven lifecycle**: validate → compile → test → package → install → deploy. `mvn package` runs all phases up to and including package.
- **Docker image** = a snapshot/blueprint. **Container** = a running instance of an image.
- **Dockerfile** = instructions to build an image: FROM (base image), COPY (add your code), RUN (execute commands), CMD (what to run).
- **docker-compose** = run multiple containers together (Spring Boot + PostgreSQL + Redis) with one command.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
- Maven: know what groupId/artifactId/version mean; know compile vs test vs provided scope.
- Maven: `mvn clean package -DskipTests` is the most common build command.
- Docker: container vs VM — containers share the OS kernel, so they are faster and lighter.
- Dockerfile: multi-stage builds produce smaller images; .dockerignore keeps layers lean.
- docker-compose: `docker-compose up -d` starts all services; `docker-compose logs -f` follows logs.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- "What is the difference between a Docker image and a container?" → Image is the blueprint (immutable); container is a running instance of that image.
- "What does the FROM instruction in a Dockerfile do?" → Sets the base image — every image starts from a parent.
- "What is dependency scope in Maven?" → compile (default, on classpath always), test (only during testing), provided (available at runtime but not packaged).
- "Why would you use docker-compose?" → To run multiple interdependent containers (Spring Boot + DB + Redis) with a single command locally.
- "What is the Maven build lifecycle?" → A sequence of phases: the most common phases are compile, test, package, install.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"I build my Spring Boot applications with Maven. I run mvn clean package to create the jar, then use a multi-stage Dockerfile — first stage compiles with Maven, second stage uses a slim JRE image and just copies the jar in. This gives me a small final image. For local development, I use docker-compose to start Spring Boot, PostgreSQL, and Redis together with a single docker-compose up. Environment-specific configuration (DB URL, passwords) is injected via environment variables — never hardcoded."*
